core_obligations: Induct on the minimal number of generators of the degree-one part, with the case of no generators settling the statement (proof lines 14121-14124).

For the induction step choose a generator, divide out by it, compare the graded pieces of the module and of the quotient degree by degree, and conclude by the numerical polynomial criterion (proof lines 14124-14160).
proof_roadmap: Induct on the number of generators of the degree-one part (proof lines 14120-14130).
Compare graded pieces along the quotient and apply the criterion (proof lines 14130-14161).
difficulty_reason: The proposition states that for a Noetherian graded ring with the positive part generated in degree one and a finite graded module, the function recording the class of the n-th graded piece is a numerical polynomial (statement lines 14106-14118). The proof does not compute Hilbert series: it inducts on the minimal number of degree-one generators, and in the induction step compares the graded pieces of the module with those of the quotient by the chosen generator, concluding by the numerical polynomial criterion (proof lines 14120-14161). Setting up the induction on that generator count is the step that makes the comparison finite. H2.
